title: Diagnostic Evaluation of Eye, Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders

headings.title: Introduction to EENT Diagnostic Evaluations
headings.content: The structures of the eye, ear, nose, and throat are compact, delicate, and deeply interconnected. Because sensory deficits profoundly impact daily life, systematic diagnostic evaluation is a core competency in nursing practice. Assessment begins with a thorough health history, exploring pain, discharge, hearing loss, visual changes, or breathing difficulties. Nurses inspect external structures for symmetry, inflammation, or trauma before specialized equipment is introduced. Understanding baseline anatomy ensures abnormal findings are recognized promptly, guiding safe and effective referrals to specialists.

headings.title: Ophthalmological Assessments and Diagnostic Tests
headings.content:
Evaluating vision and ocular health requires specific clinical tools. Visual acuity is measured using the **Snellen chart** for distance or a hand-held card for near vision. Intraocular pressure is checked via **tonometry** to screen for glaucoma, where elevated fluid pressure can damage the optic nerve. Direct and indirect **ophthalmoscopy** allows visualization of the internal retina, blood vessels, and optic disc. A **slit-lamp examination** magnifies the anterior structures of the eye, revealing corneal abrasions, cataracts, or anterior chamber inflammation.

- **Snellen chart**: Tests visual acuity by reading letters from a standardized distance.
- **Tonometry**: Measures internal eye pressure to help detect glaucoma.
- **Ophthalmoscope**: Illuminates and inspects the internal retina and optic nerve head.
- **Slit-lamp**: Uses high magnification to examine the cornea, iris, and lens.

headings.title: Otological Evaluations and Hearing Tests
headings.content:
Assessment of the ear starts with an **otoscope** to view the external ear canal and tympanic membrane. A healthy tympanic membrane appears pearly gray and translucent, with a visible cone of light. Hearing function is evaluated through both basic bedside tests and formal audiology. The **Weber test** and **Rinne test** use a tuning fork to differentiate between conductive and sensorineural hearing loss. Formal **audiometry** measures hearing thresholds across various frequencies in a soundproof booth, generating an audiogram that charts exact hearing capability.

A common misconception is that earwax impaction causes permanent sensorineural loss; in reality, cerumen buildup causes a temporary **conductive hearing loss** that resolves immediately upon irrigation or removal.

headings.title: Rhinological and Nasal Endoscopic Examinations
headings.content: Nasal and sinus evaluations uncover the causes of chronic congestion, epistaxis, anosmia, and facial pain. Physical inspection uses a nasal speculum and penlight to check mucosal color, turbinate size, and the position of the nasal septum. When deeper structures require visualization, a flexible or rigid **nasal endoscope** is utilized. Endoscopy allows the clinician to inspect the middle meatus, sinus ostia, and posterior nasopharynx for polyps, chronic inflammation, purulent discharge, or tumors.

headings.title: Throat, Laryngeal, and Pharyngeal Diagnostics
headings.content: The pharynx and larynx are assessed to investigate persistent hoarseness, dysphagia, sore throat, or airway obstruction. Examination of the oropharynx utilizes a tongue depressor and light source to inspect the tonsils, posterior pharyngeal wall, and soft palate. For laryngeal structures, **indirect laryngoscopy** uses a small warmed mirror held at the back of the throat, while **fiber-optic laryngoscopy** passes a slender scope through the nose to view the vocal cords during speech and breathing.

headings.title: Radiological and Laboratory Investigations in EENT
headings.content: Advanced imaging and lab tests complement physical examinations when disorders extend into surrounding bony or soft tissue structures. **Computed tomography (CT)** scans provide detailed cross-sectional images of the paranasal sinuses, temporal bones, and orbital sockets. **Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)** is superior for evaluating soft tissue masses, the optic nerve, and brain involvement. Laboratory studies, such as **culture and sensitivity** swabs from the throat, ear drainage, or nasal passages, identify specific bacterial or fungal pathogens driving infection.

headings.title: Nursing Responsibilities and Patient Preparation
headings.content: Nursing care during EENT diagnostics centers on patient safety, education, and comfort. Nurses must explain procedures clearly to reduce anxiety, especially when scopes or bright lights are used near the face. For exams involving topical anesthetics or mydriatic eye drops that dilate pupils, nurses must monitor for allergic reactions and warn patients about temporary blurry vision or light sensitivity. Post-procedure care includes monitoring for bleeding after nasal or throat biopsies and ensuring protective eyewear is worn until pupillary reflexes return to normal.
